checks.diagnosis: The prompt treats clause- or phrase-initial function words (articles, demonstratives, clause‑initial auxiliaries/particles) as independent cut-points, causing left-side fragments that harm cohesion or trigger contradiction.
checks.evidence: ['en_us_292','en_us_586','en_us_455','en_us_1017'] — these four cases all moved the cut so that an initial article/introductory function word is kept attached to the following content rather than left stranded, improving cohesion.
checks.type_predicate: A marker that immediately follows an initial clause- or phrase-introducing function word (an article, demonstrative, or clause‑initial auxiliary/particle) that begins the subsequent noun phrase or clause.

edit.text: Do not cut immediately after a clause- or phrase‑introducing function word (article, demonstrative, or clause‑initial auxiliary/particle); attach that function word to the following noun phrase or clause so the left side is not a stranded fragment.

orders.diagnosis: When two candidate cuts are otherwise comparable, the prompt sometimes prefers splitting a verb from its required object while keeping an earlier adjunct cut; this orders fragments badly and should prefer preserving verb+object.
orders.evidence: ['en_us_633','en_us_481','en_us_381'] — in each the measured target prefers the cut that keeps the verb and its core object/complement together (later cut), while the prompt ranked the earlier adjunct split higher.
orders.type_predicate: A sentence containing both (A) a candidate cut placed between a verb (or auxiliary) and its required object/complement and (B) another candidate cut earlier in the pre‑verbal adjunct material (time/place/manner adjunct).

edit.target: When one cut falls between a verb and its obligatory object/complement
edit.text: When comparing two cuts in the same band, if one separates a verb/auxiliary from its core object or complement and the other falls earlier inside pre‑verbal adjuncts (time, place, manner), prefer the cut that preserves the verb+object (i.e., the later cut after the complement).
